rules.covers: AI call inside a loop cost $900
background task retrying forever (approximation: flags any outbound request inside a while, does not check whether a bound exists)
who changed what: inserts into email tables must record an audit event

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Retries that run forever: no check bounds a loop's iteration count, so the rule only flags outbound requests inside a while loop
Tracking by a tag on tables holding customer email (the way the policy is meant to be scoped in the long term)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other: workspace tables have no tags; I scoped by table name instead, and the brief said not to add tags

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Confirming the audit record is correct (fields, actor), not just that the call is made
Whether an AI call costs too much per run (spend or token budget)

assumptions: 'customer emails' means the email-typed fields on customers, users, newsletter_subscribers, support_tickets (requester_email) and patients (email?)
record_audit_event is the audit function to require; it writes audit_log
ai.agent.run and api.request are the statement names for the AI call and outbound request
a while loop, foreach loop and for loop are valid must_not_be_inside block names
a predicted finding list is a prediction only; I did not run xano policy evaluate
confusions: Whether statement.containment accepts 'while' and 'for' as must_not_be_inside names: the catalogue describes foreach and try_catch as examples, but does not list the full set of block names; I assumed the loop keywords are valid and parse reported no warning

No guidance on how to express 'a loop that repeats an outbound request without a bound': the catalogue has no check for iteration counts, and the closest rule (must_not_be_inside while) is an approximation that will also flag bounded loops

No guidance on scoping a rule to write statements on named tables without a tag: object.statement_required's when takes one statement name per condition, so covering db.add, db.edit, db.patch and db.del needed four rules; a list form for when.statement would simplify this
The skill says a template prefix like AUTH- or DATA- with an unused number must not be used; it did not say whether a new prefix such as AUDIT- or COST- is acceptable, so I used those

The skill says to read policy files under /policies/ for the workspace's exemption conventions; there are none in this workspace (policy list shows none), and the skill did not say what to do when there is no convention yet
xano policy parse printed the policy back in a reformatted layout; this is useful but not documented, so I did not know whether the output or the exit code is the thing to check
wished_for: A check that bounds a loop's iteration count, or bounds the number of calls a statement can make per run (cost guard)
A complete list of block names accepted by statement.containment (for while, for, foreach, try_catch.catch, etc.)
A way to express 'statement X on table in tables list' in one rule (a list form for when.statement), instead of one rule per write statement
A template for cost controls (loop-contained AI calls, bounded retries)
Guidance on whether a new policy key prefix is acceptable when no template uses it
why_confidence: The AI-in-loop rule is a direct check of the $900 pattern and should catch it; the retry rule is an approximation (any outbound request inside a while, not an unbounded retry). The audit rules check that a record_audit_event call is unconditional for writes to the named email tables, which fits 'who changed what' only if the tables are complete and the audit call is correct; they are scoped by name, not tag, because the workspace has no table tags. Both files parse with exit 0. I did not run xano policy evaluate, so the predicted findings are unconfirmed.
